known.summary: The v4 landing text in plan-manager SKILL.md and plan-contract.md no longer tells the agent to put `Closes #<issue>` in the pull request that lands the work (and plain `Refs #<issue>` in a partial one), yet archive still accepts only a keyword closing reference (excludeUserLinked: true), so a plan landed by a pull request without the keyword can never be archived, and retire refuses the closed issue.

The shipped plan-reviewer agent says to report an unrequested temporary fix 'in the relevant goal or Spec finding' (no Spec kind exists among goal_fit, research_gap, security_risk) and also lists a temporary fix under research_gap, while the plan-reviewer skill routes it to goal_fit, so the two instructions classify the same finding differently.

parseReviewComment matches the review heading and the `Code-review:`/`Plan-review:` verdict line only at the start of the raw line, so a Markdown-formatted record (a bold `**Code-review: pass**` line, other emphasis, a quote or list marker) reads as no record: show reports code=none and archive refuses with 'archive requires Code-review: pass' although a trusted pass was posted.

table() always skips the line after the header as the separator, so a Steps or Acceptance table written without a separator row loses its first data row, and normalization writes a separator in its place; a drafting edit silently deletes the first step or acceptance criterion.

table() finds the Steps header and the row run on the raw section lines, so a fenced example table placed before the live table becomes the live table: step rewrites the example row, and archive can accept the example's done rows while the real steps stay planned.

sectionMap keys sections by canonical name and keeps only the last of two case-equivalent headings (for example `## Steps` and `## steps`), so normalization silently drops the earlier section; status or step can delete the real Steps rows, and the edit freeze checks only the surviving section.

normalizePlan takes the first `Mode:` line of Goal, including one inside a fenced code block, and deletes every Mode line, so a fenced `Mode: plan-and-implement` example above the real `Mode: plan-only` becomes the live mode, both original lines are removed, and implementation is authorized against the user's decision.

The sectionMap heading pattern `^\s*##` lets `\s*` cross newlines, so the heading match starts at the fence-masked lines before the next heading and the fenced block that ends a section is cut out; edit, status, and step silently delete a trailing fenced command or evidence block (backtick or tilde fence).

Mode discovery accepts any leading whitespace (`^\s*Mode:`), so an indented code example `    Mode: plan-and-implement` before the real `Mode: plan-only` replaces the user's decision with implementation mode, deletes the example, and prints no advice.

Dependency normalization maps each Depends entry through the step ids before the display numbers, so with a numeric step id (display 2 has id `1`) an already-normalized display number is read again as that id; successive normalizations move Depends from `prepare` to `1` to `2`, so reads and unrelated writes change the prerequisite.

table() also matches a header and rows indented four spaces or a tab (an indented code block), so an indented example Steps table before the live table is selected: its done example row becomes the plan's step state, the real planned row is ignored, archive's terminal-step check can pass with unfinished work, and normalization rewrites the example's bytes.

`new` appends the explicit `Mode: <--mode>` line after the --goal text, but normalizePlan keeps the first Mode line, so a multiline --goal that contains `Mode: plan-and-implement` overrides an explicit `--mode plan-only`, deletes the explicit decision, and publishes implementation authorization.

`new` passes --mode only as a Mode text line appended to --goal, and every body write silently drops a section with an unknown `##` heading; a --goal holding `## Context` puts the appended line into that dropped section, so even when the last Mode line wins the explicit `--mode plan-only` is lost, the goal's `Mode: plan-and-implement` is published without advice, and the goal text under the H2 disappears.

plan-manager points to the canonical checks policy, but plan-contract.md's landing section only waits up to five minutes for checks to appear; the base's rule to wait for every check to complete, block the merge question on a failed check, and handle a repository with no configured checks was dropped.
